items.text: In ti, s tistim tvojim kurčevim načinom govorjenja
items.q: Hooman calls Eskandar's way of talking 'kurčevim' (dickish) to set up the pun. Does that word sound natural?

items.text: Dež ne pada navzgor iz zemlje.
items.q: Her son says he would die for her; Maman objects. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Kaj ti je spet, da si se nam nasršil, Alain Kurčon?
items.q: Hooman mocks a roommate for getting an erection at them, using his rude nickname. Is the crude joke clear?

items.text: Sinoči se je slišalo, kako prežvekuješ.
items.q: Eskandar mocks Hooman for secretly eating sweets at night, chewing like a cow chews cud. Does 'prežvekuješ' carry that jab?
before: Eskandar se je obrnil proti Hoomanu in rekel:

items.text: Bibi, pokoj njeni duši, je v takih trenutkih govorila: če rečem, mi zgori jezik; če ne rečem, mi zgori kostni mozeg.
items.q: Maman hesitates before criticising her husband. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Ampak ga je zajebal. Orlov Pogled pravi pir tu pir, Krčmar pa Stari tu Stari.
items.q: Farid mocks Amir for hearing 'peer-to-peer' as Persian pir, elder, his nickname. Would Slovenian readers get it? If not, what word could carry it?
before: – Pošljite salavat. Starešina Krčme je končno nekaj rekel.

items.text: Naj krožim okoli tebe, jigaram. Vedno se smej.
items.q: Maman tells her son she would circle around him again and again, an old loving phrase. Does this line sound tender?
before: Nasmehnem se in poizkušam raztegniti kožo na čelu, kolikor le zmorem.

items.text: Pravi: »Dobro leto se pozna po svoji pomladi.«
items.q: The family's New Year visits were cancelled; a brother jokes about it. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: To uho je postalo gluho tudi – udaril me je in ga pustil gluhega.
items.q: Maman says he also hit her on this ear and left her deaf in it. Does this sound natural?
before: – Ženske? Rada bi. Kdor ga hoče, ga vzame zase. Damo še nekaj zraven.

items.text: zdi se mi, da moje sanje niso verjele, da si odšla
items.q: The last line of his poem to the girl he lost. Does it read as poetry?
before: a če te pot zanese mimo

items.text: Vedno zelo eleganten in slovesen, se posere prav na zgodovinskem ovinku.
items.q: Hooman says crudely that Amir, always so proper, messes up right at the crucial moment. Does this sound natural?
before: – Stari je Krčmar. Ne more si pomagati. Tako mu je tovarna nastavljena.

items.text: Morda boste rekli, da tako ne gre, da ni mogoče, da je domišljija in ni resnično. A je in vas resnično ljubim.
items.q: He insists his love is real, not a fantasy. Does 'A je' say clearly that it is real?
before: – Dvaintrideset mesecev je, kar vas ljubim. Od daleč. Ne da bi vedeli. V tišini. Brez ene besede.

items.text: S te strani odmotavam besede, ti pa jih z one strani zbiraš.
before: …te knjige. Trenutki in podobe, ki bi se izgubili v vročičnem šumu svetovnih dogodkov, če ne bi bili zapisani tukaj. Zapisani so bili, da bi postali most med mojim svetom in tvojim. Most iz mojega sveta — v trenutku, ko pišem te stavke — do tvojega, v trenutku, ko se usedeš k njihovemu branju.
